question: The strongest north-star claim: does the atlas assign mechanism to TRUE sequence-orphans (proteins structurally matchable to the atlas but <25% sequence identity to any atlas member, i.e. where sequence/BLAST transfer fails)? Scored against experimental EC labels.

orphan_scarcity.finding: Only 7/1139 (0.6%) experimentally-characterized covered-family enzymes are sequence-orphans to the atlas. Among VALIDATABLE proteins the orphan zone is nearly empty - being characterizable correlates with being sequence-reachable. The atlas's unique 'structure where sequence is blind' capability therefore rarely decides cases we can check; it presumably matters more in the uncharacterized dark proteome, which lacks ground truth.

orphan_recovery.interpretation: Existence proof: structure correctly recovered mechanism for 2 sequence-orphans (PLP @21% id TM0.74; heme @23% id TM0.85) where sequence transfer would fail. On the other 5 the atlas ABSTAINED (TM<0.70) rather than misroute - so even in the hardest regime it makes 0 confident errors (2/2 confident calls correct). Strongest claim demonstrated as existence proof (n=2), not at scale.

verdict: Atlas value over sequence baselines is REAL (twilight-zone accuracy 0.70 vs 0.28; fail-safe discrimination) and the strongest 'orphan' claim is demonstrated as a small existence proof (2/2 confident orphan calls correct) - but true orphans are rare among characterizable proteins (0.6%), so that unique capability is thinly evidenced where measurable and is a dark-proteome hypothesis where it is not.
